overview:
Alabama's first district is an open seat after redistricting reshuffled the field, and it leans Republican by 17 points. Jerry Carl, who previously represented this area in Congress, enters as the clear financial favorite, having raised $1.44 million and drawn over half a million dollars in outside support. Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. has raised about $184,000 with limited cash on hand.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and prediction markets, which price the Republican at 97 percent. The national political environment could add a few points to the Democratic side, but not nearly enough to overcome the district's lean. This race is rated Safe Republican, with the main question being the size of the winning margin rather than the outcome itself.
